claim: A labour contract can be written or verbal; if it needs registering, this is free
quote: It can be written or verbal. It can be drawn up and signed according to local custom. If it needs registering, this shall be done at no cost.

claim: A fixed-duration contract can last at most two years including renewals; breaking this rule turns it into an unlimited-duration contract
quote: The labor contract signed with consent for a specific duration cannot be for a period longer than two years. It can be renewed one or more times, as long as the renewal does not surpass the maximum duration of two years. Any violation of this rule leads the contract to become a labor contract of undetermined duration.

claim: A fixed-duration contract must be in writing, or it becomes an unlimited-duration contract
quote: A contract of a fixed duration must be in writing. If not, it becomes a labor contract of undetermined duration.

claim: Probation may last at most 3 months for regular employees, 2 months for specialised workers and 1 month for non-specialised workers
quote: the probationary period cannot last longer than three months for regular employees, two months for specialized workers and one month for non-specialized workers.

claim: A fixed-duration contract can be ended early only by written agreement of both sides in the presence of a Labour Inspector, or for serious misconduct or an act of God
quote: It can, however, be terminated before the ending date if both parties are in agreement on the condition that this agreement is made in form of writing in the presence of a Labor Inspector and signed by the two parties to the contract.

claim: If the employer alone ends a fixed-duration contract early (no serious misconduct or act of God), the worker gets damages at least equal to the pay until the contract's end
quote: entitles the worker to damages in an amount at least equal to the remuneration he would have received until the termination of the contract.

claim: If the worker alone ends a fixed-duration contract early without valid reason, the employer is entitled to damages for the harm suffered
quote: The premature termination of the contract by the will of the worker alone for reasons other than those mentioned in paragraphs 1 and 2 of this article entitles the employer to damages in an amount that corresponds to the damage sustained.

claim: For a fixed-duration contract over 6 months, the worker must be told of non-renewal 10 days ahead (15 days if over 1 year); without notice the contract is extended
quote: If the contract has a duration of more than six months, the worker must be informed of the expiration of the contract or of its non-renewal ten days in advance. This notice period is extended to fifteen days for contracts that have a duration of more than one year.

claim: At the end of any contract the worker can ask the employer for an employment certificate
quote: In every case of contract termination, the worker can require the employer to provide him with an employment certificate.

claim: Notice periods for ending an unlimited-duration contract: 7 days (under 6 months' service), 15 days (6 months to 2 years), 1 month (2 to 5 years), 2 months (5 to 10 years), 3 months (over 10 years)
quote: Seven days, if the worker's length of continuous service is less than six months; Fifteen days, if the worker's length of continuous service is from six months to two years; One month, if the worker's length of continuous service is longer then two years and up to five years.

claim: Dismissal without proper notice obliges the employer to pay wages and benefits for the notice period
quote: entails the obligation of the employer to compensate the worker the amount equal to the wages and all kinds of benefits that the worker would have received during the official notice period.

claim: No dismissal without a valid reason related to the worker's aptitude or behaviour or the enterprise's operational needs
quote: However, no layoff can be taken without a valid reason relating to the worker's aptitude or behavior, based on the requirements of the operation of the enterprise, establishment or group.

claim: During the notice period the worker gets two paid days off a week to look for a new job
quote: During the notice period, the worker of the enterprise is entitled to two days leave per week with full payment to look for a new job.

claim: Serious offences by the employer include fraud to get a worker to sign, refusing to pay all or part of wages, repeated late pay, abuse, threats or violence
quote: 1. The use of fraudulent measures to entice a worker into signing a contract under conditions to which he would not otherwise have agreed, if he had realized it; 2. Refusal to pay all or part of the wages; 3. Repeated late payment of wages; 4. Abusive language, threat, violence or assault;

claim: No notice is needed when one party commits a serious offence
quote: 2. For a serious offense on the part of one of the parties.

claim: Serious offences by the worker include theft, presenting false documents at signing, and threats or assault
quote: Fraudulent acts committed at the time of signing (presentation of false documentation)

claim: If the employer's unfair treatment or repeated contract breaches push the worker to quit, the worker can still claim indemnity and damages
quote: If the employer treats the worker unfairly or repeatedly violates the terms of the contract, he also has to pay indemnities and damages to the worker.

claim: Bankruptcy and closure of the business do not release the employer from its termination obligations
quote: Bankruptcy and judicial liquidation are not considered as acts of God.

claim: Refusing to give an employment certificate obliges the employer to pay damages
quote: The refusal to supply this certificate obliges the employer to pay damages to the worker.

claim: Wages must be paid directly to the worker, in legal currency
quote: The wage must be paid directly to the worker concerned, unless the worker agrees to get paid through other methods.

claim: The employer may not restrict how the worker uses his wage
quote: The employer, however, is prohibited from restricting the worker's freedom to using his wage at his disposal.

claim: When a contract ends, wages and any indemnity must be paid within 48 hours
quote: In the event of termination of a labor contract, wage and indemnity of any kind must be paid within forty-eight hours following the date of termination of work.

claim: In a wage dispute the employer must prove payment, through the worker's signature (or two witnesses' if illiterate) in the payroll ledger
quote: In the event of disputes over the payment of wages, the employer has the duty to prove that he has made the payment.

claim: Signing that 'all wages are paid' or accepting pay without protest does not give up the right to unpaid wages
quote: Even though the worker accepts payment without protest, this does not mean that he has renounced the right to payment of all or part of his wages

claim: A wage claim lapses three years after the wage was due
quote: A lapse of a lawsuit for the payment of wages is three years from the date the wage was due.

claim: Deducting from wages for job placement, for the employer, its representative or a labour recruiter, is prohibited
quote: Wage deductions for the purpose of job placement that are provided directly or indirectly to an employer, to his representative, or to any intermediary such as a labor recruiter are prohibited.

claim: Employer deductions are limited to unreturned tools, items in the worker's care, advances for them and company-store debts, and may never take more than the worker needs to live
quote: However, the total amount deducted from the wage, in any case, cannot surpass the portion deemed necessary to provide the basic living for the worker and his family.

claim: Normal hours may not exceed 8 a day or 48 a week
quote: the number of hours worked by workers of either sex cannot exceed eight hours per day, or 48 hours per week.

claim: No worker may be used more than six days a week; weekly rest is at least 24 consecutive hours, in principle on Sunday
quote: Weekly time off shall last for a minimum of twenty-four consecutive hours. All workers shall be given in principle a day off on Sunday.

claim: Paid annual leave is 1.5 working days per month of continuous service, plus one day per three years of service
quote: at the rate of one and a half work days of paid leave per month of continuous service.

claim: Annual leave increases by one day for every three years of service
quote: The length of paid leave as stated above is increased according to the seniority of workers at the rate of one day per three years of service.

claim: The right to take paid leave comes after one year; a contract ending earlier earns pay in place of the leave
quote: The right to use paid leave is acquired after one year of service.

claim: If the contract ends before leave is taken, the worker gets an indemnity for the leave earned
quote: If the contract is terminated or expires before the worker has acquired the right to use his paid-leave, an indemnity calculated on the basis of Article 166 above is granted to the worker.

claim: Women get 90 days' maternity leave and cannot be dismissed during it
quote: In all enterprises covered by Article 1 of this law, women shall be entitled to a maternity leave of ninety days.

claim: Maternity leave pays half wages from the employer, only for women with at least one year's service
quote: However, the wage benefits specified in the first paragraph of this article shall be granted only to women having a minimum of one year of uninterrupted service in the enterprise.

claim: Forced labour and work to pay off debts are forbidden
quote: Hiring of people for work to pay off debts is forbidden.

claim: Absence for illness certified by a doctor suspends the contract for up to six months
quote: The absence of the worker for illness certified by a qualified doctor. This absence is limited to six months

claim: No foreigner may work without a work permit and an employment card from the labour ministry
quote: No foreigner can work unless he possesses a work permit and an employment card issued by the Ministry in Charge of Labor.

claim: The work permit lasts one year and can be extended within the validity of the residence permit
quote: The work permit is valid for one year and may be extended as long as the validity of extension does not exceed the fixed period in the residency permit of the person in question.

claim: The labour ministry can revoke a work permit when the holder is unemployed for more than a month or is hired by another employer
quote: When the holder is unemployed for more than one month or is hired by another employer.

claim: An individual dispute can first go to the provincial or municipal Labour Inspector for conciliation
quote: Prior to any judicial action, an individual dispute can be referred for a preliminary conciliation, at the initiative of one of the parties, to the Labor Inspector of his province or municipality.

claim: An agreement reached before the Labour Inspector is legally enforceable; parties can be assisted or represented
quote: An agreement made before the Labor Inspector is enforceable by law.

claim: If conciliation fails, the party has two months to file in court, or the claim lapses
quote: In case of non-conciliation, the interested party can file a complaint in a court of competent jurisdiction within two months, otherwise the litigation will be lapsed.

claim: Hiring or keeping a foreigner without an employment card: fine of 61 to 90 days' base daily wage or 6 days to 1 month's jail for the employer
quote: Any person who hires or keeps in his service a foreigner, who does not possess the employment card authorizing him to carry out a paid job in the Kingdom of Cambodia, is liable to a fine of sixty-one to ninety days of the base daily wage or to imprisonment of six days to one month.

claim: Overtime is paid at 150% of normal pay, and 200% at night or on the weekly day off
quote: the overtime hours shall be paid at a rate of fifty percent higher than normal hours. If the overtime hours are worked at night or during weekly time off, the rate of increase shall be one hundred percent.

claim: From 1 January 2027 the minimum wage in textiles, garments, footwear, travel goods and bags is USD 212 a month for regular workers and USD 210 for probationers (Prakas 226/26 of 30 September 2026)
quote: Regular workers/employees: USD 212 per month

claim: Probationary garment-sector workers get at least USD 210 a month from 1 January 2027
quote: Probationary workers/employees: USD 210 per month

claim: Piece-rate workers whose output pay falls below the minimum must be topped up to it
quote: If their output-based earnings fall below the applicable minimum wage, the employer must pay the difference

claim: A temporary transport and accommodation allowance of USD 2.50 a month continues in 2027
quote: the temporary transportation and accommodation allowance of USD 2.50 per month, established by the decision dated 20 March 2026, will continue to apply in 2027.

claim: In 2026 the garment-sector minimum wage is USD 210 a month for regular workers and USD 208 for probationers (Prakas 214/25)
quote: for regular workers, USD 210 per month; and (2) for probationary workers, USD 208 per month.

claim: Garment-sector workers also get USD 7 a month transport or accommodation allowance, USD 10 attendance bonus, USD 0.5 a day meal allowance (or a free meal) for overtime, and a USD 2 to 11 seniority bonus
quote: such as compensation for a transportation or accommodation allowance of USD 7 per month, an attendance bonus of USD 10 per month, a meal allowance of USD 0.5 per day (or one free meal per day) for workers who work overtime and a seniority bonus from USD 2 to USD 11

claim: The statutory minimum wage covers only garment, textile, footwear, travel goods and bag manufacturing; other industries have none
quote: Yes, the minimum wage law currently applies only to the garment, textile, footwear, and travel goods sectors. Other industries are not subject to this mandated minimum wage.

claim: Since 2019, workers on unlimited-duration contracts get a seniority payment of 7.5 days' wages and benefits in June and 7.5 days in December (15 days a year), replacing the old dismissal indemnity
quote: 7.5 days of the employee’s wages and other fringe benefits, to be paid in June of each year; and

claim: Workers on fixed-duration contracts get no seniority payment but severance of 5% of the wages for the contract's length
quote: Employees hired under a specific duration contract (an employment contract with a fixed start and end date) will not receive the seniority payment, but are entitled to severance pay, calculated at 5% of the wages the employee would have received during the length of the contract

claim: Prakas 442 (2018) requires pay twice a month from January 2019: 50% in the second week and the rest plus benefits in the fourth week
quote: Must be made in the second week of the month and consist of 50% of the employee’s actual wages for the month

claim: A worker who resigns before the end of June or December loses that half-year's seniority payment; no seniority indemnity is due on resignation or dismissal for serious misconduct
quote: However, if the employee resigns before the end of June or December, he/she will not be eligible for the payment.

claim: The seniority payment is paid with the second wage payment of June and December
quote: The seniority indemnity will be paid together with wages in the second payment of June and December.

claim: The probation period does not count toward seniority
quote: The employment period begins after the employment agreement is signed and the employee is hired on a full-time basis, exclusive of any probation period.

claim: Under Prakas 112/25 (6 May 2025) overtime must be voluntary and cannot be forced through coercion or discipline
quote: However, the overtime work must be conducted voluntarily and must not be enforced through coercion or disciplinary action.

claim: Overtime may not take total hours over 10 a day except for disaster prevention or repair
quote: overtime must not cause total working hours to exceed 10 hours per day, except in cases of disaster prevention or rectification.

claim: Overtime pay: 150% in daytime on working days; 200% from 10 pm to 5 am and on weekly days off
quote: 150% or one-and-a-half times the normal wages for overtime work conducted during the daytime on regular working days; 200% or twice the normal wages for overtime work conducted from 10 p.m. to 5 a.m. (overnight) and on weekly days off

claim: Work on paid public holidays is voluntary
quote: employees may be requested to perform work on paid public holidays on a voluntary basis.

claim: After night overtime the employer must provide accommodation or transport
quote: employers must provide appropriate accommodation or transportation to employees following nighttime overtime work.

claim: Employers must file overtime on MLVT's LACMS system at least three working days ahead, with a confirmation signed or thumbprinted by two-thirds of staff representatives or over half the workers involved
quote: A confirmation letter signed or thumbprinted by either two-thirds of the staff representatives or by over 50% of the total employees involved.

claim: Cambodia's 2026 paid public holidays (Anukret 167 and MLVT Prakas 216) include Khmer New Year 14-16 April, Pchum Ben 10-12 October and the Water Festival 23-25 November
quote: Khmer New Year

claim: Since the 2021 amendment of Article 162, a public holiday falling on a Sunday no longer gives a substitute day off
quote: Under the amended Article 162 of the Labour Law, workers no longer get a substitute day off when a public holiday falls on a Sunday.

claim: A full-time worker earns 18 working days of annual leave per 12 months
quote: This means 18 working days for 12 months of service.

claim: The Labour Law gives no paid sick leave; ministry policy is 100% pay in the first month, 60% in the second and third, unpaid from the fourth to sixth
quote: The Labour Law does not provide for paid sick leave; however, following the policy of the Ministry of Labour, employers may provide paid sick leave as follows: - 100% of wages during the first month of sick leave; - 60% of wages during the second & third months of sick leave; and - unpaid leave from the fourth to the sixth month.

claim: Instruction 015/25 requires the employer to pay the 50% maternity wages in full before leave starts; NSSF pays 70% for 90 days to women with 9 months' contributions in the last 12
quote: now requires employers to pay all due wages in full (i.e., 50%) before the worker starts her maternity leave.

claim: NSSF pays 70% of reference earnings for 90 days to a woman with 9 months' contributions in the last 12
quote: An employee who has 9 months of contribution in the last 12 months is granted 70% of the reference earnings for 90 days from Social Security (NSSF).

claim: Every enterprise with one or more workers must register with NSSF, and all paid workers, Cambodian and foreign, are covered
quote: All workers, both Cambodian and foreigner, are employed at the enterprise/establishment with wages.

claim: NSSF members get free care at health facilities with an NSSF agreement (NSSF logo)
quote: The NSSF member have entitlement to access medical care services free of charge at the health facility signed the agreement with NSSF.

claim: Absence for sickness, accident or maternity with a prescription over 7 consecutive days earns 70% of contributory wage from NSSF, up to 180 days in 12 months
quote: for over 7 (seven) consecutive days, he will receive 70% of his contributory wage from NSSF

claim: The daily allowance needs health-care contributions for 2 consecutive months or 6 months in the last 12
quote: Employer has paid contributions of Health Care for 2 consecutive months or at least 6 months within the last 12 months

claim: After a work injury, NSSF pays 70% of contributory wage from the second day until recovery; the employer pays the first day
quote: the victim concerned will receive 70% of his contributory wage starting from the second day of accident until recovery.

claim: A caretaker of an injured worker gets 50% of the worker's daily allowance
quote: a caretaker of victim will also receive 50% of victim's daily allowance for temporary disability.

claim: Permanent disability under 20% is paid as a lump sum; 20% or more as a monthly pension
quote: in case the victim has permanent disability from 20% up, NSSF provides monthly pension.

claim: If a work injury kills the worker, NSSF pays body transport and 4 million riels to whoever holds the funeral
quote: Provide 4 million riels to person who is responsible for holding the funeral.

claim: NSSF takes responsibility for corpse transportation cost after a fatal work injury
quote: Take responsibility for corpse transportation cost

claim: Survivors' benefit claims need a family record book, residence certificate, marriage certificate or copy
quote: Eligibility: All beneficiaries must have family record book, certificate of residency, marriage certificate, or a copy of marriage certificate.

claim: After a work injury the employer must inform NSSF at once on 1286 and send the work-injury form within 48 hours, directly or to benefit@nssf.gov.kh
quote: In case the worker has work injury, employer must inform NSSF immediately via 1286

claim: Work-injury forms go to NSSF directly or to benefit@nssf.gov.kh within 48 hours
quote: benefit@nssf.gov.kh in a qualifying period of 48 hours

claim: Claims for daily allowance and funeral grant after a work injury are valid for 1 year; permanent disability for 5 years
quote: Entitlement to daily allowance and funeral grant due to work injury is valid for 1 year, while entitlement to permanent disability benefits is valid for 5 years.

claim: Foreign workers attach their passport and NSSF card to benefit claims
quote: for the foreigner and the NSSF membership card of victim.

claim: If asked to pay at an NSSF facility, show the NSSF card and call 1286; in an emergency call 1286 for an ambulance
quote: If you are required to pay the service cost, please call 1286.

claim: NSSF pays benefit cheques: it calls the worker within 20 to 30 working days to collect the cheque
quote: NSSF will contact you through the given phone number within 20 to 30 working days at the latest in order to pick up the cheque

claim: NSSF keeps original documents; workers should keep copies
quote: Please make a copy of all documents and keep a set for yourself (worker) because NSSF requires all original copies in order to process claims.

claim: NSSF headquarters: Building 3, Russian Federation Blvd, Tuek Laak I, Toul Kork, Phnom Penh (MLVT compound); info@nssf.gov.kh; 1286
quote: Building 3, Russian Federation Blvd, Sangkat Tuek Laak I, Khan Toul Kork, Phnom Penh (in the compound of the Ministry of Labour and Vocational Training).

claim: A worker who changes job stays covered for work injury only if the new employer registers him
quote: If worker changes job, he is still covered by Occupational Risk Scheme if his new employer registers him at NSSF.

claim: Employers must register workers with NSSF within 3 days of hiring, using the passport for foreign workers
quote: no later than 3 (three) days from the date of employment except workers/employees who have been registered.

claim: A foreigner who enters Cambodia clandestinely, by fraud or other illegal means faces 3 to 6 months' prison before being expelled (Law on Immigration 1994, Art. 29)
quote: be subjected to imprisonment for three to six months prior to his being expulsed out of the

claim: Falsifying, lending or using under another name a resident card, work card or employment contract, or filing a fake application for them, carries 5 to 15 years' prison (Law on Immigration 1994, Art. 32)
quote: files a fake application for these above documents, shall be subjected to imprisonment for a term of five (5) to fifteen (15) years

claim: The Minister of Interior may expel any foreigner working in Cambodia without a work card (Law on Immigration 1994, Art. 36)
quote: working in the Kingdom of Cambodia without a labor/working card

claim: An expulsion order takes effect at once; the person may complain to the court within two months (Law on Immigration 1994, Art. 38)
quote: The concerned person shall have rights to file complaint to the court within a period of two (2) months

claim: Expulsion is carried out within 7 days of the Minister of Interior's decision unless a court suspends it (Law on Immigration 1994, Art. 39)
quote: The expulsion shall be carried out within 7 days, after an official decision is made by the

claim: Owners or occupiers of any dwelling must tell the authorities within 24 hours that a foreigner is staying there (Law on Immigration 1994, Art. 18)
quote: within 24 hours, of the presence of any immigrant or non-immigrant aliens

claim: Fines are imposed by the Ministry of Interior, and expulsion can be added to any penalty under the Law on Immigration (Art. 33-34)
quote: additional other sub-punishments including the expulsion from the territory of the Kingdom of Cambodia

claim: Under MLVT Guideline 517 (17 January 2023), a labour inspector may fine an employer KHR 12.6 million (about USD 3,150) per foreign employee working without a work permit
quote: being KHR12.6 million (approximately USD 3,150) per foreign employee

claim: Where five or more foreign employees lack work permits, the maximum administrative fine is KHR 63 million
quote: If there are five or more foreign employees working without work permits, the labour inspector may impose a maximum administrative fine of KHR 63 million

claim: Foreign employees working without a work permit face up to three months' prison and/or deportation under the Law on Immigration
quote: provide for a term of imprisonment of up to three months and/or deportation orders for the foreign employees concerned

claim: Keeping, transporting or trafficking Table I or II narcotics carries 2 to 5 years' prison and a fine of 4 to 10 million riels (Law on Drug Control 2012, Art. 40)
quote: in Table I and Table II shall be punishable by imprisonment from 2 (two) years to 5 (five) years. In addition, the offender may be held liable by a fine from 4,000,000

claim: Larger quantities (for example 15 to 80 grams of methamphetamine, amphetamine or ecstasy) carry 5 to 10 years' prison (Law on Drug Control 2012, Art. 40)
quote: Methamphetamine, amphetamine or ecstasy with a pure quantity from 15
note: The 5-10 year band is stated in the same article: 'Shall be punishable by imprisonment from 5 (five) years to 10 (ten) years'

claim: Using Table I or II narcotics carries 1 to 6 months' prison and a fine of 100,000 to 1,000,000 riels (Law on Drug Control 2012, Art. 45)
quote: shall be punishable by imprisonment from 1 (one) month to 6 (six) months and may be held liable by a fine from 100,000 (one hundred thousand) Riels to 1,000,000

claim: Cambodia's Law on Combating Online Scams was promulgated by Royal Decree on 6 April 2026
quote: On April 6, 2026, the Royal Government of Cambodia promulgated a Royal Decree announcing the Law on Combating Online Scams

claim: Committing a technology-enabled scam carries 2 to 5 years' prison and a fine of KHR 200 million to 500 million
quote: Offenders are subject to 2 to 5 years of imprisonment and fines ranging from KHR200 million to KHR500 million

claim: Scams by an organised group or against many victims carry 5 to 10 years' prison and KHR 500 million to 1 billion
quote: penalties increase to 5 to 10 years of imprisonment and fines ranging from KHR500 million to KHR1 billion

claim: Recruiting or training others to take part in online scams carries 2 to 5 years' prison
quote: Anyone who recruits or trains others to participate in technology-enabled scams will be subject to 2 to 5 years of imprisonment

claim: Collecting or using identity cards or passports to facilitate online scams carries 1 to 3 years' prison and KHR 100 million to 300 million
quote: is punishable by 1 to 3 years of imprisonment and a fine ranging from KHR100 million to KHR300 million

claim: Running a scam centre with violence, unlawful detention or exploitation carries 10 to 20 years' prison; if someone dies, 15 years to life
quote: the offender will be subject to 10 to 20 years of imprisonment

claim: Overstaying a Cambodian visa costs USD 10 a day in fines, and deportation procedures can take more than six months
quote: sparing citizens from daily fines of USD 10, and shortening deportation procedures that would otherwise take more than six months

claim: Cambodia waived overstay fines for 4,677 Indonesians in 2026 so they could go home
quote: a total of 4,677 Indonesians has now benefited from Cambodia’s policy of lifting penalties for overstaying visas

claim: The overstay fine has traditionally been about USD 10 a day, settled at the airport on departure
quote: The traditional overstay fine was about $10 per day. It was historically settled at the airport on departure.

claim: A viral notice claiming two years' jail and an USD 8,000 fine for foreigners from 1 June 2026 was a forgery; the Ministry of Interior rejected it on 29 May 2026
quote: Cambodia's Ministry of Interior rejected it on May 29

claim: According to the Nepali Embassy in Bangkok (May 2026), Cambodia's new legal provisions allow arrest, fines and prison for foreigners who fail to leave within one month
quote: new legal provisions allow authorities to arrest, fine and imprison foreign nationals who fail to leave the country within one month

claim: A sub-decree of January 2026 fines owners or managers of guesthouses, apartments, dormitories, factories and similar premises 4 million riels (USD 1,000) for each foreigner staying illegally
quote: fined four million riel (US$1,000) for each illegal resident

claim: Under the January 2026 sub-decree, premises must ask foreigners for documents proving their legal right to stay before letting them stay, and give resident lists to the commune within 24 hours
quote: they must require foreigners to present documents proving their legal right to stay in Cambodia

claim: Bangladesh has no embassy in Cambodia; the Bangladesh mission in Bangkok handles consular work for Cambodia
quote: কম্বোডিয়ায় বাংলাদেশের কোনো দূতাবাস নেই। দেশটিতে বাংলাদেশের কনস্যুলার কার্যক্রম পরিচালনা করে ব্যাংককে অবস্থিত বাংলাদেশ মিশন।

claim: On 3 September 2026 Cambodian immigration police detained 32 Bangladeshis at Phnom Penh airport as they tried to leave
quote: সেদিন কম্বোডিয়ার রাজধানী নমপেনের বিমানবন্দরে দেশ ছাড়ার চেষ্টার সময় ৩২ বাংলাদেশিকে আটক করে দেশটির অভিবাসন পুলিশ।

claim: Cambodian authorities interviewed Bangladeshis applying to go home to screen for trafficking victims; those identified as victims were allowed to leave
quote: যাদের মানব পাচারের শিকার হিসেবে শনাক্ত করা হয়েছে, তাদের দেশে ফেরার অনুমতি দেওয়া হয়েছে।

claim: The detained Bangladeshis had to pay for their own tickets home
quote: তাদের দেশে ফেরার টিকিটের খরচ নিজেদেরই বহন করতে হবে।

claim: The bodies of three Bangladeshis were brought home from Cambodia on 8 October 2026
quote: গত ৮ অক্টোবর কম্বোডিয়া থেকে তিন বাংলাদেশির মরদেহ দেশে আনা হয়।

claim: Bangladesh's Bangkok mission received requests about 1,796 Bangladeshis stranded in Cambodia; about 350-400 had returned since July 2026
quote: গত জুলাই থেকে প্রায় ৩৫০ থেকে ৪০০ বাংলাদেশি দেশে ফিরেছেন।

claim: Cambodia's visa-overstay fine waiver for these Bangladeshis was due to expire on 31 October 2026
quote: a visa-overstay fine waiver expires on Oct 31

claim: The 30 Bangladeshis held in a Cambodian immigration centre returned to Dhaka on 20 October 2026, after more than six weeks in detention
quote: ছয় সপ্তাহেরও বেশি সময় পর আজ তারা ঢাকায় ফিরেছেন।

claim: On arrival in Dhaka, the CID (Criminal Investigation Department) ran forensic checks on the returnees and their phones
